pairs.difference: A: the asteroid is a violet-grey mass with almost no chroma of its own, and only the small pink crystals carry color. It sits on a one-hue orange burst, so the card is two families, with subject chroma and hue count both below the real range and warm share above it. B: the bouncy house has yellow, orange and red on a cyan-blue burst. Its slightly high hue count comes from small steps inside the warm range, so hero and background still read as real hue roles.
pairs.fix: Give the rock warm brown and ochre patches with cool grey-blue in the craters, make the crystals a stronger magenta, and add a cooler blue-violet band to the orange background.

pairs.difference: A: the swing ride has saturated red and yellow on violet, with the chains in muted blue, a clear warm hero on a cool ground. B: the keyboard has pure red, neutral white keys and a grey stand on blue, with small multi-color buttons as the accent. Both have the loud hero-on-ground split of the real cards. B's duller shadows are a small deviation but give no color reason to choose.

A: the white-grey station, panels, sky and planet all fall in blue, with only a thin orange ring and a small green land patch. Warm share is near zero, hue count is below the real range, the background is louder than the hero, and the lens reduces the whole card to blue and white. B: the red bike and pale blue car sit against a peach and yellow sunset, with brown saddle and grips as local colors and dark plum shadows. Its hue count runs high, but warm and cool masses are balanced like a real scene card.
pairs.fix: Lower the blue of the space background toward deep navy, make the hull warm cream with rust-orange and red panels, and enlarge the warm accent so it is more than a thin line.

pairs.difference: A: the cream scroll with red ribbon and gold seal lies on a saturated cyan and navy table. B: the cream sheet with blue line drawings lies on orange wood against violet. Both creams lean warm and both keep rich shadow color. A's glossy blue table is less natural than B's wood, but its cream, red and gold hero against blue is a valid real-style role split, so color does not separate them.

A: the tiki bar has many local colors, including straw, dark wood, green stools, turquoise water and fruit accents. It has a high hue count, but each color belongs to a material. B: the rocket is pale grey and red against a dusty denim sky and flat olive-green grass. The background hues are muted and greyish compared with the clean blues and greens on real scene cards, and the red is the only strong note.
pairs.fix: Make the sky a clean bright blue, the grass a fresh yellow-green, the rocket body warm white with soft blue reflections, and add yellow or orange flame-colored details.

pairs.difference: A: a neutral silver tube stands on a flat magenta wall and a grey-lilac shelf. The card is nearly one hue plus grey, the only accents being the red cap and a thin green stripe, and hue count is below the real range. Subject chroma sits at the bottom of the range, so the background overpowers the hero. B: the blue vending machine on violet is cool overall, but pink, yellow, green and red cans give it the small multi-hue payload real cards use.
pairs.fix: Tint the tube with a colored printed label covering much of its body, use a yellow or green cap accent, and shift the background to a two-tone pattern so magenta stops dominating.

pairs.difference: A: the observatory has a cobalt dome, lilac-pink stone, gold telescope, peach-orange sky, pink clouds and acid-green hills. Every zone is a different family, the hue count is above the real range, and there is no rest area, with the lens splitting the wall into pink, sage and yellow patches. B: the sandcastle stays in one warm sand family with a teal sea, and the green bucket and blue spade are clear accents.
pairs.fix: Keep the sky to one soft blue, paint the stone a single warm grey, keep the hills one calm green, and leave the gold telescope and blue dome as the only strong colors.

pairs.difference: A: this is the same rose arch that appears on the real reference sheet, with pink on pink stripes and deep green leaves, so it is real. B: the backpack has lime and grass green with brown leather straps and a blue roll on a red-orange diamond background. It is loud but local colors hold, with the leather reading brown and chroma, warm share and shadow values inside real ranges. Nothing on my vector marks it as generated.

A: the balloons are orange, red, teal and violet in a pale sky with neutral white clouds. The soft background is below the real range on chroma, but the white clouds rest the eye. B: the cobalt globe with a copper-orange stand sits on a saturated green diamond pattern, with three pure hues and little neutral, though its numbers are inside the real range. Each departs from real cards in a different way, and neither departure is decisive.

A: the ice-blue comet sits on violet wave bands. There is no warm color anywhere, warm share is 0, and the background chroma is above the real range and louder than the hero, so the card reads as cool on cool. B: the red scarf on cyan swirls is very saturated, but the gold badge gives a warm accent and the red-against-blue role split matches real cards.
pairs.fix: Add a warm orange-yellow glow at the comet's head and tail, make the ice slightly paler and whiter in its lit faces, and darken and mute the violet background so the comet stands out.

pairs.difference: A: the plant has acid yellow bulbs, lime-green stems, a violet pot, a cyan wall and an orange table, all at similar high chroma, with no neutral or muted area. The lens breaks the stems into scattered yellow, sage and plum bits. B: the teal book on orange wood has a single complementary pair, plus stickers and a cream page edge as resting colors, though its shadow leans brick red.
pairs.fix: Use one soft green for the plant and warm pale yellow bulbs, make the pot a muted terracotta or dusty plum, and calm the wall to a soft pale blue.

pairs.difference: A: the capsule's metal is steel-blue with no true neutral, and its underside is a saturated indigo, set on a yellow rings background, with one red stripe. The blue pushed through the gray matches the generated cameras in the lessons. B: the envelope is natural warm cream with small multi-color postcards on a very saturated green. That green is above the real range, but the hero's local colors are believable. The call is weak because A's numbers are inside the real range.
pairs.fix: Paint the metal a true neutral grey with warm yellow bounce from the background on the lower edge, and make the underside a dark charcoal instead of indigo.

pattern: Generated cards tend to lose the balance of hue roles in one of two ways. Some collapse into a single family, with a near-neutral or same-hue hero on a background louder than it (asteroid on orange, station in blue, tube on magenta, comet on violet). Others fill every zone with an equally loud, different hue and leave no neutral rest (observatory, plant). Across the lessons and test pairs, gray metal is pushed toward blue and cream toward yellow or peach instead of staying a true neutral local color. Warm accents, when present, are thin lines rather than real masses, and backgrounds are cleaner and more saturated than real ones. Real cards keep a neutral or naturally colored hero with one clear contrast against the ground, plus small accents.
